title: Resilience handshakes, backward compatibility, and deprecation paths for Python/TS/Go SDKs
creator: Asha Patel
description: This PRD defines required client-side behaviors and acceptance criteria for Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) to ensure resilient, predictable interactions with the Redwood Inference platform across versions and feature rollouts. Focus areas: graceful degradation when server features change, unified pagination token contract, deterministic retry semantics for streaming and non-streaming endpoints, connection handshake for streaming/backpressure, and a clear deprecation/compatibility policy for SDKs and server APIs.
scope: MUST: define token-based paging contract, idempotency keys and retryability rules, streaming handshake and backpressure signals, and a compatibility matrix. SHOULD: provide migration helpers, automated compatibility checks in CI, and sample integration tests. MAY: runtime feature flags to toggle new protocols for canary customers.
requirements: Paging: server returns 'next_cursor' (opaque string) and 'prev_cursor' when applicable; SDKs expose cursor-forward APIs and an iterator abstraction that hides low-level token handling.
Paging: SDK iterator must support optional page_size hint and stop-on-duplicate-detection to avoid infinite loops if server returns repeated cursors.

Retries: define idempotency semantics per endpoint. Non-stream text generation endpoints: retries allowed for 5xx and network errors when idempotency key provided. Streaming endpoints: retries are allowed only before stream establishment; once token frames delivered, client must surface non-idempotent failure to application.

Streaming handshake: introduce a lightweight pre-flight 'capabilities' exchange: client sends supported-protocol-versions header and preferred-compression; server responds with selected-protocol-version and backpressure-window size. SDK must negotiate and fall back to previous protocol when server selects older version.
Backpressure: streaming SDKs must honor server-sent 'window' updates and pause read loops when window exhausted; provide user-configurable max-concurrent-bytes and event for 'throttled' state.

Compatibility: SDKs must accept an informational 'X-Redwood-MinServerVersion' header and include 'X-Redwood-SDK-Version' on every request. SDKs must map server-chosen features to runtime behavior via a feature matrix maintained in the release notes.

Deprecation policy: when server removes or changes a feature, it will provide a deprecation window (>= 90 days) and a transitional compatibility mode; SDKs must expose a 'compatibility_mode' opt-in for the older behavior for the deprecation window.

Integrations and tests: provide e2e test suites for pagination loops, retry scenarios with injected failures, streaming handshake negotiation and backpressure simulation; CI must run compatibility matrix tests against the latest runtime and the previous two runtime versions.
Docs: include migration guide highlighting common breaking changes and recommended code snippets for Python/TS/Go.
Telemetry: emit structured telemetry events for protocol negotiation failures, retry churn counts, and pagination loops > N pages (configurable threshold).
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose a high-level paginated iterator in each language with identical observable behavior: next_page(), next_item(), and an async streaming equivalent where applicable.

In controlled failure tests, non-streaming endpoints with idempotency keys must succeed after a retry injected at the transport layer 95%+ of the time without duplicated outputs (within test tolerance).

Streaming handshake negotiation must be covered by an integration test matrix that asserts SDK falls back to server-selected protocol version and honors server backpressure window in >99% of test runs.
Deprecation opt-in: when server toggles compatibility_mode=true in response to header, SDK must route to legacy behavior for the duration of the simulated deprecation window.
CI must include a daily compatibility job that validates SDK client calls against the runtime-previous and runtime-current images; any regression must open ENG tickets automatically.
Public docs and migration guide published before SDK changes reach GA and linked from SDK changelogs.
Telemetry for negotiation and retry metrics are logged and visible in the Redwood Console experimental dashboard for the SDK-compat project.
Performance targets: SDK iterator overhead does not add more than 5ms per page on average in microbenchmarks for common page_size values (100, 500, 1000).
risks: Complex handshake increases coupling between client and server; risk of deadlocks if backpressure windows are mishandled by early SDK implementations.
Opaque cursors can hide server bugs that cause cursor loops; require guardrails in SDK to avoid infinite iteration.
Retries for streaming scenarios are subtle; incorrect assumptions may lead to duplicated outputs or user-visible inconsistent state.
Maintaining compatibility matrix increases release overhead across three SDKs and multiple runtime versions.
Telemetry volume and privacy: shipping detailed negotiation telemetry requires vetting PII-safe fields and potentially opt-outs for enterprise customers.
decisions: Use opaque string cursors (no client parsing) with server-provided next_cursor/prev_cursor semantics.
Implement handshake as an HTTP upgrade/initialization request for WS and an initial JSON exchange for chunked streaming; both follow the same version negotiation headers.
Retry policy default: exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 attempts for non-stream idempotent calls. Streaming session establishment: max 1 retry before surfacing to app.
Expose compatibility_mode flag in SDK constructors and an environment variable override for rapid testing.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): design and spec published, language leads implement iterator and basic retry semantics. Phase 2 (3 weeks): handshake + backpressure implementations and integration tests. Phase 3 (2 weeks): CI matrix, docs, migration guides, and canary release to 10% of customers. Phase 4: GA and telemetry monitoring for 30 days with automatic rollback criteria (error rate > 1% on canary).
